quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The commercial bank's internal audit discovered that front-line staff had been routinely mis-selling payment protection insurance to customers who did not need or could not benefit from it. The bank self-reported to the Financial Conduct Authority before the regulator had initiated any inquiry. The FCA accepted the self-referral as a mitigating factor in determining the size of the financial penalty.
options: Internal audit discovered systematic PPI mis-selling by front-line staff.
The bank self-reported to the FCA before any regulatory inquiry had begun.
The FCA accepted self-reporting as a mitigating factor in setting the penalty.
The bank concealed the mis-selling and denied all regulatory wrongdoing.
quests.hint: Follow the compliance story: discovering wrongdoing, self-reporting, then mitigation. One frame replaces transparency with concealment.
quests.explanation: Regulatory compliance narratives show internal discovery, proactive self-reporting, and mitigated penalty. The distractor replaces transparency with deliberate concealment.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The behavioural economist conducted a randomised controlled trial in which one group of energy consumers received personalised consumption data compared with similar households, while the control group received only their standard bill. Those who received the comparison data reduced consumption by twelve per cent. The intervention was adopted nationally by the energy regulator.
options: The RCT found no statistically significant difference between the two groups.
An RCT compared personalised consumption data against standard billing.
Those receiving comparison data reduced consumption by twelve per cent.
The energy regulator adopted the intervention nationally.
quests.hint: Trace the behavioural trial: the RCT design, the significant finding, then national adoption. One frame removes statistical significance.
quests.explanation: Behavioural economics narratives show a controlled experiment, a significant finding, and national policy adoption. The distractor removes the finding.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The civil servant drafted a briefing paper on the risks of procuring critical national infrastructure from foreign state-owned entities and submitted it to the permanent secretary. The permanent secretary escalated the briefing to the relevant minister. The minister commissioned a cross-departmental security review.
options: The civil servant drafted a risk briefing on foreign state infrastructure procurement.
The permanent secretary escalated it to the relevant minister.
The permanent secretary decided the briefing was alarmist and filed it without escalation.
The minister commissioned a cross-departmental security review.
quests.hint: Sequence the civil service story: drafting, escalating, then commissioning a review. One frame stops at the permanent secretary's desk.
quests.explanation: Civil service narratives show drafting, escalation, and ministerial commissioning of a review. The distractor stops the escalation by having the permanent secretary dismiss the briefing.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The independent production company pitched an original drama series based on an underreported historical injustice to a major streaming platform. The platform commissioned a six-episode series following a detailed script development process. The series received three BAFTA nominations in its first year.
options: The company pitched a drama series on an underreported historical injustice.
The streaming platform rejected the pitch as too niche for its audience.
The platform commissioned six episodes after detailed script development.
The series received three BAFTA nominations in its first year.
quests.hint: Follow the creative production story: pitching, commissioning after development, then awards recognition. One frame replaces commissioning with rejection.
quests.explanation: Creative industry narratives show pitching, commission after development, and critical recognition. The distractor removes the commission and the recognition.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The environmental law clinic at the university provided pro bono legal advice to a small community group challenging the planning permission for a polluting industrial facility near their homes. The clinic's lawyers identified procedural flaws in the planning authority's decision. The High Court quashed the planning permission on those grounds.
options: The law clinic provided pro bono advice to a community challenging a polluting facility.
Lawyers identified procedural flaws in the planning authority's decision.
The High Court quashed the planning permission on those grounds.
The High Court dismissed the community's case on all grounds.
quests.hint: Trace the legal challenge: providing advice, identifying flaws, then the court's decision. One frame has the court dismiss the case.
quests.explanation: Environmental justice narratives show pro bono legal support, identifying procedural failures, and a successful judicial outcome. The distractor has the court dismiss the case.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The neuroscientist's lab published findings showing that a specific pattern of deep brain stimulation reduced the frequency of treatment-resistant depressive episodes by sixty per cent. The paper underwent peer review at two journals before being accepted. It subsequently attracted five million pounds in further research funding.
options: The peer review process found significant methodological flaws and rejected the paper.
The lab published findings on deep brain stimulation reducing depressive episodes by sixty per cent.
The paper was peer reviewed at two journals before acceptance.
The publication attracted five million pounds in further research funding.
quests.hint: Sequence the research story: publishing the finding, peer review, then the funding outcome. One frame uses peer review to reject the paper.
quests.explanation: Research publication narratives show findings, peer review, and further funding. The distractor turns peer review into a rejection based on flaws.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The local authority's adult social care team identified a pattern of self-neglect cases that had been classified as low-risk and closed without follow-up, several of which had subsequently resulted in serious harm. It commissioned a case review to examine how the risk assessment tool had been applied. The review found that caseload pressures had led practitioners to systematically underestimate risk.
options: Adult social care identified a pattern of closed low-risk cases resulting in serious harm.
A case review was commissioned to examine the risk assessment tool's application.
The review concluded the risk assessment tool had been applied correctly throughout.
The review found caseload pressures had led to systematic risk underestimation.
quests.hint: Follow the case review: identifying a pattern of harm, commissioning a review, then the finding. One frame removes the finding of error.
quests.explanation: Safeguarding review narratives show identifying a pattern, commissioning a review, and finding systemic underestimation. The distractor removes the finding and clears the process.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The data journalist built a database of planning decisions for a hundred English councils over five years and found a statistically significant correlation between the political affiliation of the planning committee and decisions on applications for social housing. She published her methodology and full dataset alongside the article. Two academic researchers subsequently replicated her findings.
options: The journalist built a database finding a correlation between political affiliation and social housing decisions.
Academic researchers were unable to replicate her findings using her dataset.
She published her methodology and full dataset alongside the article.
Two academics subsequently replicated her findings.
quests.hint: Trace the data journalism story: building the database, publishing openly, then independent replication. One frame removes replication.
quests.explanation: Data journalism narratives show analysis, open methodology, and academic replication. The distractor removes the independent confirmation of the findings.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The public health nurse noticed a cluster of measles cases in a neighbourhood with low vaccine uptake. She arranged an emergency vaccination clinic at a local community centre and worked with community leaders to address concerns. Vaccination coverage in the neighbourhood rose from fifty to eighty-five per cent within six weeks.
options: The nurse noticed a measles cluster in an area with low vaccine uptake.
She arranged an emergency clinic and worked with community leaders on concerns.
Vaccination coverage rose from fifty to eighty-five per cent in six weeks.
The measles outbreak spread to neighbouring areas before it could be contained.
quests.hint: Sequence the outbreak response: noticing the cluster, emergency intervention, then measurable improvement. One frame replaces containment with spread.
quests.explanation: Outbreak response narratives show early detection, targeted community intervention, and a measurable rise in coverage. The distractor replaces containment with uncontrolled spread.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The financial regulator identified a systemic vulnerability in the risk models used by several mid-sized banks to calculate their capital requirements. It required all affected institutions to stress-test their models against three adverse scenarios. One institution failed the stress test and was required to raise additional capital within six months.
options: All institutions passed the stress tests and no further action was required.
The regulator identified a systemic vulnerability in banks' risk models.
It required stress-testing against three adverse scenarios.
One institution failed the stress test and was required to raise additional capital.
quests.hint: Follow the supervisory story: identifying the vulnerability, stress-testing, then the outcome. One frame removes the failure.
quests.explanation: Prudential regulation narratives show identifying risk, stress-testing, and enforcement action where failure occurs. The distractor removes failure and the subsequent enforcement.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The playwright received a commission from a national theatre company to write a new play exploring the experience of undocumented migrants in a major city. She spent six months conducting research, including interviews with individuals who had lived experience of irregular migration. The premiere received widespread critical praise for its authenticity and emotional power.
options: The playwright received a commission to write about undocumented migrants.
She spent six months researching, including interviews with those with lived experience.
The theatre withdrew the commission following a political controversy.
The premiere received widespread praise for its authenticity and emotional power.
quests.hint: Trace the creative story: the commission, immersive research, then the premiere's reception. One frame removes the premiere through withdrawal.
quests.explanation: Commissioned theatre narratives show receiving a commission, rigorous research, and critical acclaim at premiere. The distractor removes the premiere through political withdrawal.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The council introduced a selective licensing scheme for private landlords in a high-density rental area following evidence of widespread property standards failures. Landlords were required to register and meet minimum standards to obtain a licence. Within two years, the proportion of properties meeting minimum standards had risen from sixty to ninety per cent.
options: The council introduced selective licensing for landlords following evidence of property failures.
Most landlords refused to register and the scheme was declared unenforceable.
Landlords were required to register and meet minimum standards for a licence.
Properties meeting standards rose from sixty to ninety per cent within two years.
quests.hint: Sequence the licensing story: introducing the scheme, the requirement to register and meet standards, then the improvement. One frame replaces improvement with non-compliance.
quests.explanation: Housing regulation narratives show introducing licensing, compliance requirements, and measurable improvement. The distractor replaces improvement with widespread non-compliance.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The technology company's engineers identified a zero-day vulnerability in its cloud storage platform that could allow unauthorised access to user files. They patched the vulnerability and deployed the fix before any exploit had been detected in the wild. The company issued a transparency report disclosing the vulnerability and its resolution to users.
options: Engineers identified a zero-day vulnerability in the cloud storage platform.
They patched and deployed the fix before any exploit was detected.
The company issued a transparency report disclosing the vulnerability and resolution.
The vulnerability was exploited by attackers before the company discovered it.
quests.hint: Follow the cybersecurity story: identifying the flaw, patching before exploitation, then transparent disclosure. One frame reverses the timing by having the vulnerability exploited first.
quests.explanation: Cybersecurity narratives show proactive discovery, pre-exploitation patching, and transparent disclosure. The distractor reverses the story by placing exploitation before discovery.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The transport secretary announced a review of urban speed limits, citing evidence that lower limits significantly reduced pedestrian and cyclist fatalities. The review consulted local authorities, transport professionals, and road safety charities. It recommended a default twenty miles per hour limit in all residential areas.
options: The review found insufficient evidence to change any existing speed limits.
The transport secretary announced a speed limit review citing safety evidence.
The review consulted local authorities, transport professionals, and road safety charities.
It recommended a default twenty mph limit in all residential areas.
quests.hint: Trace the policy review story: the announcement, consultation, then the recommendation. One frame removes the recommendation by finding insufficient evidence.
quests.explanation: Policy review narratives show an evidence-based announcement, a consultative process, and a clear recommendation. The distractor removes the recommendation.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The community development charity trained twenty local residents to become mental health first aiders in a socially deprived neighbourhood with high rates of anxiety and depression. Trained residents ran monthly drop-in sessions from a converted shop unit. Referrals to the GP surgery for mental health support fell by a third in the first year.
options: The charity trained twenty local residents as mental health first aiders.
Residents ran monthly drop-in sessions from a converted shop unit.
The trained residents found it too difficult to sustain the sessions and stopped.
GP referrals for mental health fell by a third in the first year.
quests.hint: Sequence the community health story: training, running sessions, then measurable impact. One frame removes the impact through unsustainability.
quests.explanation: Community health narratives show training local people, sustained peer-led delivery, and a measurable reduction in professional referrals. The distractor removes sustainability and impact.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The university's research ethics committee received an application to conduct a study involving covert observation of members of the public in a shopping centre. The committee found that the research design did not meet the informed consent requirements of the institution's ethical framework. It rejected the application and required the researchers to redesign the methodology.
options: The ethics committee received an application for covert observation in a shopping centre.
The ethics committee approved the study despite the informed consent concerns.
It found the design failed informed consent requirements.
The committee rejected the application and required a redesigned methodology.
quests.hint: Follow the ethics review: the application, finding the ethical failure, then the rejection and requirement to redesign. One frame approves despite the concerns.
quests.explanation: Research ethics narratives show an application, ethical review finding a failure, and a protective rejection. The distractor approves the flawed study despite identified concerns.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The health secretary published a national obesity strategy that shifted the policy emphasis from individual responsibility toward the structural determinants of diet, including advertising, food environment, and pricing. The food industry lobbied against the advertising restrictions. The restrictions were included in the final legislation after a parliamentary amendment.
options: The health secretary published a strategy focusing on structural determinants of obesity.
The food industry lobbied against the proposed advertising restrictions.
Advertising restrictions were included following a parliamentary amendment.
The advertising restrictions were dropped following industry lobbying.
quests.hint: Trace the policy story: the strategy, industry lobbying, then inclusion of restrictions. One frame has the lobbying succeed in removing the restrictions.
quests.explanation: Health policy narratives show a structural strategy, industry opposition, and legislative retention of key measures. The distractor allows industry lobbying to succeed in removing the restrictions.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The human rights lawyer spent three years gathering evidence that migrants detained in an immigration removal centre had been subjected to degrading treatment. She brought proceedings before the domestic courts and lost at first instance. The European Court of Human Rights subsequently upheld her case and awarded compensation.
options: The European Court of Human Rights declined to hear the case.
The lawyer spent three years gathering evidence of degrading treatment of detained migrants.
She brought domestic proceedings but lost at first instance.
The European Court of Human Rights upheld her case and awarded compensation.
quests.hint: Sequence the human rights story: gathering evidence, domestic failure, then ECHR success. One frame removes the ECHR outcome.
quests.explanation: Human rights litigation narratives show evidence gathering, domestic failure, and international vindication. The distractor removes the international remedy.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The coroner's inquest into the death of a young man in police custody heard evidence over four weeks from police officers, custody staff, medical personnel, and independent witnesses. The jury returned a conclusion of unlawful killing. The Independent Office for Police Conduct announced it would conduct a criminal investigation.
options: The coroner's inquest heard four weeks of evidence from multiple witnesses.
The jury returned a conclusion of unlawful killing.
The jury returned a conclusion of death by natural causes.
The IOPC announced a criminal investigation following the inquest.
quests.hint: Follow the inquest story: hearing evidence, the jury's conclusion, then the investigation. One frame changes the verdict.
quests.explanation: Inquest narratives show evidence-gathering, a jury conclusion, and a consequent investigation. The distractor reverses the verdict.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The local clinical commissioning group identified that mental health patients in its area were significantly less likely to receive physical health checks than the general population. It ran a targeted outreach programme through community mental health teams to increase uptake. Physical health monitoring rates for this group rose to near-parity with the general population within two years.
options: The CCG found mental health patients received fewer physical health checks.
The disparity in physical health checks remained unchanged despite the programme.
A targeted outreach programme via community mental health teams was run.
Physical health monitoring rates rose to near-parity within two years.
quests.hint: Trace the health equity story: identifying the disparity, running an outreach programme, then achieving near-parity. One frame removes the improvement.
quests.explanation: Health equity narratives show identifying a disparity, targeted intervention, and near-elimination of the disparity. The distractor removes the improvement.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The international criminal court issued an arrest warrant for a former head of state accused of crimes against humanity committed during an internal conflict. The country hosting the accused refused to extradite him, citing diplomatic immunity. The ICC pursued alternative measures to restrict the accused's international travel and financial assets.
options: The ICC issued an arrest warrant for a former head of state.
The host country refused extradition citing diplomatic immunity.
The ICC pursued measures to restrict travel and financial assets.
The accused voluntarily surrendered to the ICC and faced trial.
quests.hint: Sequence the international law story: issuing a warrant, the host country's refusal, then alternative measures. One frame removes the obstruction with voluntary surrender.
quests.explanation: International criminal law narratives show issuing a warrant, state non-compliance, and pursuing alternative enforcement. The distractor removes state obstruction.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The consumer rights organisation conducted mystery shopping exercises at fifty car repair garages and found that thirty per cent had overcharged customers or recommended unnecessary work. It published the findings alongside a guide to consumer rights when using car repair services. The Competition and Markets Authority announced a market study into the sector.
options: The mystery shopping found all garages were operating honestly and fairly.
Mystery shopping found thirty per cent of garages overcharged or recommended unnecessary work.
The organisation published findings alongside a consumer rights guide.
The CMA announced a market study into the car repair sector.
quests.hint: Follow the consumer protection story: finding wrongdoing, publishing, then regulatory action. One frame clears all garages.
quests.explanation: Consumer protection narratives show finding evidence of overcharging, publishing with guidance, and triggering regulatory investigation. The distractor removes the evidence of wrongdoing.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The national park authority commissioned a drone survey of moorland damaged by wildfire to assess the scale of vegetation loss. The survey data was combined with soil carbon measurements taken by a team of ecologists. The results were used to design a targeted moorland restoration programme covering twelve hundred hectares.
options: A drone survey assessed vegetation loss from moorland wildfire damage.
Drone data was combined with soil carbon measurements from ecologists.
The survey found the moorland had recovered naturally without intervention.
Results were used to design a targeted restoration covering twelve hundred hectares.
quests.hint: Trace the ecological assessment story: the drone survey, combining data, then informing the restoration programme. One frame removes the need for intervention.
quests.explanation: Ecological assessment narratives show remote sensing, combining data sources, and informing a targeted restoration programme. The distractor removes the need for restoration.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The secondary school's behaviour team analysed referral data and found that a small number of students with undiagnosed sensory processing difficulties were disproportionately represented in exclusion statistics. The school arranged diagnostic assessments and put in place sensory-adapted environments for those students. Exclusions among that group fell to zero within a year.
options: Analysis found students with undiagnosed sensory difficulties were over-represented in exclusions.
Exclusion rates among those students remained unchanged despite the interventions.
The school arranged assessments and provided sensory-adapted environments.
Exclusions among that group fell to zero within a year.
quests.hint: Sequence the inclusion story: identifying the pattern, intervention, then the outcome. One frame removes the improvement.
quests.explanation: Educational inclusion narratives show data-driven identification, targeted intervention, and elimination of exclusions. The distractor removes the positive outcome.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The city's flood risk management plan was found by an independent review to have relied on outdated sea level rise projections that did not reflect the latest climate science. The city commissioned revised modelling based on updated IPCC projections. The revised plan identified an additional thirty thousand properties at risk that had not appeared in the original assessment.
options: An independent review found the flood plan used outdated sea level projections.
Revised modelling was commissioned based on updated IPCC projections.
Thirty thousand additional at-risk properties were identified in the revised plan.
The revised modelling confirmed the original assessment was accurate.
quests.hint: Follow the planning review story: finding outdated projections, commissioning updated modelling, then the finding. One frame confirms the original assessment.
quests.explanation: Climate risk planning narratives show identifying outdated assumptions, commissioning updated analysis, and a significantly expanded risk finding. The distractor confirms the original rather than expanding the risk picture.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The professional association's accreditation committee conducted a site visit to a training provider and found significant discrepancies between the curriculum it had approved and the curriculum being delivered to students. It issued the provider with a formal notice of concern and required an action plan within thirty days. The provider submitted a satisfactory action plan and was given conditional accreditation.
options: The accreditation committee withdrew the provider's accreditation immediately.
The committee found discrepancies between the approved and delivered curriculum.
It issued a formal notice of concern requiring an action plan within thirty days.
A satisfactory action plan was submitted and conditional accreditation was given.
quests.hint: Trace the accreditation story: finding discrepancies, issuing a formal notice, then conditional accreditation. One frame replaces conditional accreditation with immediate withdrawal.
quests.explanation: Quality assurance narratives show finding discrepancies, issuing a formal notice, and a proportionate conditional outcome. The distractor replaces a proportionate response with immediate withdrawal.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The public defender took on the appeal of a client who had pleaded guilty to robbery under duress from her co-defendant and without proper legal advice. She gathered testimony from a witness who had been present when the co-defendant threatened the client. The court of appeal quashed the conviction and entered an acquittal.
options: The defender took on a client who had pleaded guilty under duress without proper advice.
She gathered testimony from a witness who witnessed the co-defendant's threats.
The court of appeal dismissed the appeal and upheld the original conviction.
The court of appeal quashed the conviction and entered an acquittal.
quests.hint: Sequence the appeal story: taking the case, gathering witness testimony, then the court's outcome. One frame has the court dismiss the appeal.
quests.explanation: Miscarriage of justice appeal narratives show re-examination, new evidence, and a successful quashing. The distractor has the court uphold the conviction.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The product liability lawyer received instructions from three hundred claimants who alleged they had suffered identical adverse reactions to a prescribed drug. She instructed toxicologists and epidemiologists to establish causation. Following a four-year litigation, the manufacturer settled for two hundred million pounds.
options: The lawyer received instructions from three hundred claimants with adverse drug reactions.
The case collapsed when experts failed to establish causation.
She instructed toxicologists and epidemiologists to establish causation.
The manufacturer settled for two hundred million pounds after four years.
quests.hint: Follow the mass tort story: receiving instructions, expert evidence for causation, then settlement. One frame collapses the case at the expert stage.
quests.explanation: Mass tort litigation narratives show receiving instructions, establishing causation through experts, and a large settlement. The distractor removes the causation finding and collapses the case.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The national broadcaster's editorial board reviewed its coverage of climate change over a five-year period and found it had given disproportionate airtime to climate sceptic voices relative to the scientific consensus. It published its findings as part of an annual impartiality report. It updated its editorial guidelines to require that climate sceptic voices be identified as representing a minority position.
options: The board found disproportionate airtime had been given to climate sceptic voices.
It published its findings in the annual impartiality report.
Editorial guidelines were updated to identify sceptics as representing a minority position.
The board found its coverage accurately reflected the scientific consensus.
quests.hint: Trace the editorial accountability story: identifying the imbalance, publishing findings, then updating guidelines. One frame removes the finding of imbalance.
quests.explanation: Editorial accountability narratives show self-assessment, transparent publication, and guideline reform. The distractor removes the finding of imbalance that drove the reform.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The museum education team identified that school visit numbers had declined sharply following the introduction of admission charges six years earlier. It proposed reinstating free admission for all school groups as a pilot. Following the one-year pilot, school visit numbers returned to their pre-charge levels.
options: The pilot free admission scheme failed to attract more schools.
The team identified that school visits had declined sharply since admission charges were introduced.
It proposed reinstating free admission for school groups as a one-year pilot.
School visits returned to pre-charge levels following the pilot.
quests.hint: Sequence the access story: identifying declining visits, proposing free admission pilot, then the recovery. One frame makes the pilot fail.
quests.explanation: Cultural access narratives show identifying a barrier, a pilot removal of the barrier, and recovery of engagement. The distractor makes the pilot ineffective.
